context.requirement_text:
Closes part 1 of ISS-0431/GH#835 (queue task 431): Letflow has no
admission control or backpressure anywhere. ISSUE-FIXER's diagnosis
(handoffs/WF03-ISS0431-20260902/step-01-issue-fixer-diagnosis.json)
confirmed by direct read that no bounded-concurrency mechanism exists
on any surface -- lib/letflow/plugs/api_pipeline.ex's plug chain has
none (Letflow.Plugs.RateLimit is a different, still-unmounted S4
mechanism -- request-RATE throttling, not concurrency admission --
porting it would not close this gap); lib/letflow/application.ex's
five Task.Supervisors all bound unrelated subsystems (sandbox
provisioning, plugin/Lua/Wasm dispatch), none of them HTTP-request or
Poller concurrency against the Ecto pool; config/runtime.exs:113 sets
`pool_size` from `POOL_SIZE` with nothing anywhere referencing it.
Four prior issues (ISS-0194, ISS-0219, ISS-0222, ISS-0224) each solved
a DIFFERENT local instance of the same root cause (unbounded demand vs.
a bounded connection resource) with no shared mechanism; this
requirement is the shared mechanism, so a fifth ad hoc shape does not
get invented. THIS REQUIREMENT IS THE CORE ONLY -- no HTTP-path or
Poller wiring (REQ-217, REQ-218), mirroring REQ-186/REQ-214's own
"core module first, wiring requirements second" split precedent in
this file.

DECISIONS RESOLVED HERE (ISS-0431's own "TO DECIDE, not prescribed"
list), with reasoning, not left to ELIXIR-DEV to improvise:

1. LIBRARY VS. HAND-ROLLED: hand-rolled, pure-BEAM GenServer-based
counting semaphore(s). No new dependency. Reasoning transferred
directly from decision 0014 (new-dependency policy), which the
diagnosis already checked: 0014's method is to ask whether a pure-BEAM
option removes the hazard class outright vs. merely mitigating it, and
to treat any new native/NIF dependency as a real, disclosed cost
requiring its own comparison. Bounding concurrent access to Ecto
connections is a problem the BEAM's own primitives already solve
natively (a GenServer counter, `:queue` + monitors -- the same shape
`Letflow.SandboxPool`, REQ-039/ISS-0224, already uses for an adjacent
but distinct problem) with no NIF surface at all, so 0014's own
argument for preferring pure-BEAM mechanisms applies here with no
countervailing benefit to a hex dependency (this is a small, fully
in-house state machine, not a mature external sandboxing runtime the
way wasmex's Wasmtime binding is).

2. GLOBAL VS. PER-TENANT VS. BOTH: BOTH, composing, not either alone.
A per-tenant-only cap cannot bound total demand on `pool_size` (N
tenants each admitted up to a per-tenant cap can jointly exceed
`pool_size` the same way ISS-0194's N-partitions-times-pool_size math
already demonstrated for a structurally identical multiplication). A
global-only cap cannot stop one tenant's burst starving every other
tenant, which ISS-0431 itself names as "arguably the more important
property in a multi-tenant BPM platform" and which is exactly decision
0006's multi-tenancy isolation posture (schema-per-tenant data
isolation composed with NO existing resource-fairness isolation) --
leaving it unaddressed would be a real regression against that
posture, not a neutral omission. So: a GLOBAL semaphore bounds total
admitted concurrent DB-connection-holding work platform-wide, and a
PER-TENANT semaphore (one counter per active tenant schema, entries
created lazily on first admission attempt, never pre-allocated for
every possible tenant) bounds any single tenant's share of that same
budget. Default per-tenant share: an equal fair-share split of the
global cap across the CURRENTLY-DISTINCT tenants that have made an
admission attempt in a rolling window (avoids the global cap collapsing
to 1 the instant tenant count exceeds it -- floor of 1 slot per tenant,
matching decision 0009/ISS-0194's own "clamp with a floor" precedent),
overridable per environment. Tier-weighted per-tenant caps (e.g. a
paying tenant getting a larger share) are explicitly OUT OF SCOPE and
recorded as a genuinely open product question, not resolved here:
`Letflow.Identity.Tenant`'s schema (lib/letflow/identity/tenant.ex) has
no plan/tier field to weight by (verified by reading the schema block
in full -- only `slug`, `display_name`, `status`, `idp_realm_id`
exist), so introducing tenant tiering is a genuine product decision
with no existing data model to hang it on, not an implementation
detail this requirement can quietly decide. Equal fair-share is the
only defensible default absent that decision.

3. TIE TO POOL_SIZE/MAX_CONNECTIONS (closing the drift ISS-0194/0219/
0222/0224 already show happens between independently-tuned numbers):
the global cap MUST be expressed as a function of the configured Ecto
`pool_size` (config/runtime.exs's `POOL_SIZE`/`config :letflow,
Letflow.Repo, pool_size:` -- read the SAME value this module reads,
never a second independently-set number), specifically
`pool_size - reserved_headroom`, where `reserved_headroom` (config,
default 2) reserves connection budget for non-admission-controlled
DB consumers this requirement does not touch (REQ-186's
`Letflow.Scheduler.Poller` before REQ-218 wires it in;
`Letflow.SandboxPool`'s own already-serialized DB worker; migrations).
This function relationship, not a hardcoded number, is the
acceptance-tested contract -- changing `POOL_SIZE` at boot changes the
computed global cap on the very next boot with no second setting to
update, closing exactly the drift class this issue exists to end.

4. RESPONSE SHAPE: settled by existing precedent, not invented here.
`Letflow.Api.Response.service_unavailable/2` (REQ-066,
lib/letflow/api/response.ex) already exists, is already used for an
analogous resource-exhaustion rejection
(`lib/letflow/routers/promotions.ex`'s "no sandbox free within
timeout"), and REQ-066's own moduledoc documents the caller-sets-
Retry-After convention identically to `rate_limited/2`. This
requirement's core module returns a typed outcome the wiring
requirements (REQ-217/218) map onto that EXISTING response helper --
this requirement does not touch any router or plug itself (no HTTP
surface in scope), so it does not call `Response.service_unavailable/2`
directly, but its return-type design must make that mapping a
one-line call, not require the caller to reconstruct rejection
semantics.

NOT ABSORBED, WITH REASON: ISS-0224's own deferred
`Letflow.SandboxPool` admission-shaped defect (its `handle_call/3`
blocking the pool mailbox during synchronous provisioning) is a
DIFFERENT resource -- ephemeral promotion-pipeline sandbox slots, not
the tenant-request-serving Ecto pool -- already has its own
independently-reasoned wait-queue/slot-bookkeeping shape (REQ-039,
ISS-0048's crash-reclaim invariants), and was deliberately scoped out
of its own parent fix (ISS-0220 §12) specifically to avoid conflating
two independently-revertable subsystems. Folding it into this
cross-cutting core module now would repeat exactly that mistake in
reverse. It stays a separate, still-open concern; REQ-039/ISS-0224's
module is prior art for the wait-queue SHAPE (a FIFO of waiters with
per-waiter timeout, ISS-0224's own fix for exactly that shape) that
this requirement's per-tenant/global semaphores may reuse internally,
but is not the same mechanism and is not touched by this requirement.

SCOPE:
1. New module `Letflow.Admission` (or equivalently named per its own
moduledoc) plus a supervised GenServer (or a small set of them --
state the shape chosen and why in the moduledoc) implementing:
`try_acquire(pool :: :global | {:tenant, tenant_schema :: String.t()}) ::
{:ok, admission_ref()} | {:error, :capacity}` and
`release(admission_ref()) :: :ok`. No HTTP or Poller-specific
vocabulary anywhere in this module -- REQ-217/218 are the only
callers, and both are equally valid callers of the exact same API.
2. Global cap computed once at supervised-child start from
`Application.fetch_env!(:letflow, Letflow.Repo)[:pool_size]` (the
SAME config key `config/runtime.exs` already writes) minus
`reserved_headroom` (config, default 2), never re-read from a second
independently-configured value.
3. Per-tenant cap computed as the equal fair-share split described in
decision 2 above, with a floor of 1 and recomputed as the set of
currently-tracked tenants changes (a tenant with zero admission
attempts in the tracking window is not counted against the split).
4. `try_acquire/1` for `{:tenant, _}` MUST also consume one unit of
the SAME global budget (both gates are checked, not just the
per-tenant one) -- decision 2's own "both, composing" requirement made
concrete and testable.
5. Added to `Letflow.Application`'s supervision tree
(lib/letflow/application.ex), following this file's own established
Task.Supervisor-ordering discipline (state explicitly in the moduledoc
whether any other child must start before or after it, or that no
ordering dependency exists, mirroring REQ-173/REQ-166's own "no
ordering dependency" precedent comments in application.ex).
NOT IN THIS REQUIREMENT: no plug, no route, no change to
api_pipeline.ex or poller.ex (REQ-217, REQ-218); no tier-weighted caps
(recorded above as a genuinely open product question); no change to
`Letflow.SandboxPool` (a different resource, explicitly not absorbed,
see above).

task.description: WF-02 Step 3b RE-CHECK: independently verify TEST-DESIGNER's rework of the idempotent-release test (step-06) genuinely closes the vacuous-test gap raised in step-05, by direct reading and by reproducing the exact mutant myself (not trusting TEST-DESIGNER's quoted output).
acceptance_criteria: test/letflow/admission_test.exs's 'release/1 is idempotent on an unknown/already-released ref' test asserts post-release STATE (:sys.get_state or an equivalent behavioral proof), not just the :ok return value, for both the double-release and forged-ref cases

TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR independently reproduces the exact mutant class from step-05 (the {:release,...} handle_call clause always decrementing global_in_use using caller-supplied ref data, regardless of state.refs membership) and confirms the strengthened test now fails against it, with real quoted output from its own run -- not copied from TEST-DESIGNER's report
after reverting the independently-applied mutant, the full test file passes clean (15/15) with real quoted output, and git status confirms zero residual diff on lib/ and test/
no other test in the file regressed or was altered outside the one strengthened test
the full-suite Lua/PlatformTest failure characterization (unrelated flakiness) is sanity-checked for plausibility (no code relationship between admission.ex/admission_test.exs and Lua/REQ-161 code)

result.summary:
Re-checked TEST-DESIGNER's rework (handoffs/WF02-REQ216-20260902/step-06-test-designer-rework.json) independently, not by trusting its quoted output.

1. READ the updated test directly (test/letflow/admission_test.exs:137-171, 'release/1 is idempotent on an unknown/already-released ref'). Confirmed: it captures state_after_real_release = :sys.get_state(name) right after the one real release; after the second (already-released) release it asserts :sys.get_state(name).global_in_use == state_after_real_release.global_in_use; after releasing a hand-constructed forged ref (%Admission.Ref{id: make_ref(), pool: :global}) it asserts the same equality again; and it closes with a behavioral proof independent of internal field names -- with the test's pool_size dropped from 4 to 3 (reserved_headroom 2, cap exactly 1), exactly one further :global try_acquire succeeds and the next is rejected. This is no longer a return-value-only assertion.

2. INDEPENDENTLY REPRODUCED the exact step-05 mutant myself (did not copy TEST-DESIGNER's report). Confirmed git status --porcelain lib/ test/ was clean before starting. Edited lib/letflow/admission.ex's {:release,...} handle_call clause myself: changed the match to bind the caller-supplied `pool` field (`{:release, %Ref{id: id, pool: pool}}`), removed the Map.pop nil-branch guard, and made it unconditionally decrement global_in_use and call release_tenant(state.tenants, pool) regardless of whether `id` was a live member of state.refs. Ran `mix test test/letflow/admission_test.exs` myself (toolchain required `source ~/.asdf/asdf.sh` first -- mix is an asdf shim, not directly on PATH):
   Result (mutant applied): '1) test AC4: release frees exactly the budget(s) it was acquired against release/1 is idempotent on an unknown/already-released ref (Letflow.AdmissionTest) / test/letflow/admission_test.exs:137 / left: -1 / right: 0 / test/letflow/admission_test.exs:155' -- 'Result: 14/15 passed' / 'Failed: 1 test'. Exactly and only the strengthened test fails, as intended -- it now catches the state corruption (global_in_use going negative) that the old return-value-only assertion missed entirely.

3. REVERTED my own mutant (`git checkout -- lib/letflow/admission.ex`). Confirmed `git status --porcelain lib/ test/` is empty (clean). Re-ran `mix test test/letflow/admission_test.exs`: 'Result: 15 passed' -- matches the pre-mutation baseline I also ran myself before applying the mutant ('Result: 15 passed').

4. Confirmed via `grep -c '^  test\|^    test' test/letflow/admission_test.exs` that the file still has exactly 15 tests (matches step-05's baseline of 15; no test count regression), and confirmed by reading step-06's diff description that no other test or lib/letflow/admission.ex code changed outside the one test.

5. Sanity-checked the full-suite Lua/PlatformTest characterization: grep -in 'lua\|platform' over lib/letflow/admission.ex returns only two false-positive substring matches ('evaLUAted' inside the moduledoc's prose, at lines 31 and 67) -- zero real references to Lua or platform code. admission_test.exs has zero matches at all. Confirms admission.ex/admission_test.exs have no code relationship to Letflow.Engine.Lua.PlatformTest (REQ-161), consistent with TEST-DESIGNER's flakiness characterization being plausible. Did not repeat the full 1500s suite run myself, per instructions.

All five acceptance criteria for this re-check are independently verified. The step-05 gap is genuinely closed: the test now discriminates the exact defect class it is meant to guard against, proven by my own independently-applied and independently-reverted mutation, not by trusting TEST-DESIGNER's report.

VERDICT: PASS.
